there is no evidence to support the use of SMBG in the management of people with type 2 DM.
the use of SMBG in type II diabetes is a very important tool in the management of the disease.

(i) there are insufficient data available to make a recommendation for or against the routine use of SMBG in patients with type-2 diabetes, (ii) the use of SMBG may be justified in patients with type‐2 diabetes who are on insulin or oral hypoglycaemic agents (OHA), and (iii) the use of a SMBG may be beneficial for patients on OHA who are at risk of hypoglycaemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of SMBG in type II diabetes is not cost-effective.
the use of SMBG in type II diabetes is associated with increased healthcare costs.
the use of SMBG in patients with type 2 diabetes on diet and exercise, or diet and exercise plus metformin, is unlikely to be cost‐effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of SMBG in type-2 diabetes patients has a significant impact on the cost of care.
the costs of self‐monitor‐ing of blood glucose in type 2 diabetics are high and that these costs are not justified by any improvement in outcomes.
